info.text: Unit 1 — Navigating maintenance documentation by ATA chapter. CEFR B2. Listening, reading, use of English and vocabulary.

questiontext.text:
Listen to Dialogue 1 again. Rita says the AMM lists every task the manufacturer approves for this aircraft.

True or false?

generalfeedback.text: The AMM (Aircraft Maintenance Manual) lists every approved task and gives the steps. That is exactly what Rita tells the new technician.

feedback.text: Correct — the AMM is the manual that holds all the approved tasks.
Listen again — Rita says the AMM lists every task the manufacturer approves.

questiontext.text: Listen to Dialogue 1 again. What does page block 401 always mean?

generalfeedback.text: Each page block holds one type of work. Block 401 always means removal and installation — that is why the tyre-change task sits there.

feedback.text: Correct — block 401 is removal and installation.
No — that kind of work sits in a different page block, not 401.
No — block 401 is removal and installation, not fault finding.
No — block 401 is removal and installation.

questiontext.text: Listen to Dialogue 1 again. The full task number is "thirty-two, forty-one, oh-one". Write the ATA chapter number as a figure.

generalfeedback.text: The landing gear is ATA chapter 32 on every aircraft type. It is the first pair of digits in 32-41-01.

feedback.text: Correct — chapter 32 is the landing gear.

questiontext.text: Listen to Dialogue 2 again. What does the lead say you must read first, before the warnings and cautions?

generalfeedback.text: Always read the effectivity first — it tells you which aircraft the task applies to. If it does not match your tail number, you stop.

feedback.text: Correct — the effectivity comes first, before warnings and cautions.

answer.text: The revision number in the header

feedback.text: You do check the revision, but the lead says the effectivity comes first.
No — you read the whole task after the effectivity, warnings and cautions.
No — the IPC is for part numbers, not the first thing to read on a task.

questiontext.text:
Listen to Dialogue 2 again. A caution protects people from injury.

True or false?

generalfeedback.text: A caution protects the aircraft or the equipment from damage. A warning protects people. People first, hardware second.

feedback.text: Correct — a caution protects the aircraft; a warning protects people.
Listen again — the box that protects people is the warning, not the caution.

questiontext.text: Listen to Dialogue 4 (the announcement) again. Which AMM revision went live overnight? Write the number as a figure.

generalfeedback.text: AMM revision 47 went live overnight, so the team must pull the current task cards from the terminal and close last week's printouts.

feedback.text: Correct — revision 47.

questiontext.text: Listen to Dialogue 4 (the announcement) again. For how many of the team's aircraft has the effectivity on chapter 32 changed? Write the number as a figure.

generalfeedback.text: The lead says the effectivity on chapter 32 has changed for two of the team's aircraft, so the technicians must check before they start.

feedback.text: Correct — two aircraft.

questiontext.text: Listen to Dialogue 3 again. According to the mentor, what happens once a service bulletin is embodied?

generalfeedback.text: A service bulletin can change an AMM task. As soon as it is embodied, you follow the new instructions in the manual.

answer.text: It changes the steps you follow in the AMM

feedback.text: Correct — once embodied, you follow the new AMM instructions.

answer.text: It becomes a mandatory order from the aviation authority

feedback.text: No — that describes an airworthiness directive, not a service bulletin.

answer.text: It cancels the aircraft technical log record entirely

feedback.text: No — the tech log record is not cancelled by a service bulletin.

answer.text: It replaces every airworthiness directive on the type

feedback.text: No — a service bulletin does not replace airworthiness directives.

questiontext.text:
Read the MEL extract.

MEL item 33-51 — One cabin reading light may be inoperative for up to 3 days (Category C), provided the item is placarded and the defect is recorded in the tech log.

For how long may the reading light stay inoperative?

generalfeedback.text: The MEL (Minimum Equipment List) says whether the aircraft may fly with an item unserviceable, and for how long. Here the limit is up to 3 days.

feedback.text: Correct — the extract gives a limit of up to 3 days.

answer.text: Until the next scheduled maintenance check

feedback.text: No — the extract gives a fixed limit of 3 days, not the next check.

answer.text: For an unlimited period, with no time limit

feedback.text: No — the MEL always sets a time limit; here it is 3 days.

answer.text: Only until the end of the current flight

feedback.text: No — the limit is up to 3 days, not a single flight.

questiontext.text:
Read the tech log entry.

TECH LOG — 07 AUG. Defect: nose-wheel tyre worn beyond limit. Action: tyre replaced per AMM 32-41-01. Work order WO-4471 raised and signed.

The tech log entry records both the defect and the action taken. True or false?

generalfeedback.text: The tech log is the aircraft's record of defects and completed work. This entry states the defect (worn tyre) and the action (tyre replaced), with the work order.

feedback.text: Correct — it records the defect and the action.
Read again — the entry gives the defect and the action taken.

questiontext.text:
Read the work order.

WORK ORDER WO-4471 — Replace nose-wheel tyre, aircraft MSN 0451. Refer to AMM 32-41-01. Return parts data to stores.

What does the work order tell the technician to do?

generalfeedback.text: The work order gives the instruction (what to do) and points to the AMM task for the method (how). It does not contain the steps itself.

answer.text: Carry out the tyre replacement, using the AMM task

feedback.text: Correct — do the job and follow AMM 32-41-01 for the method.

answer.text: Design a brand-new tyre-change procedure from scratch

feedback.text: No — the method already exists in the AMM task the order points to.

answer.text: Decide whether the aircraft is airworthy enough to fly

feedback.text: No — that is the MEL's job, not the work order's.

answer.text: Write the maintenance manual for the whole landing gear

feedback.text: No — the AMM already exists; the work order just points to a task in it.

questiontext.text:
Read the BITE readout.

BITE READOUT — ATA 34 (Navigation). Fault code 34-11: NAV display, no data. Recommended action: refer to AMM 34-11-00; wiring check per IPC figure 34-11-07.

The BITE readout points the avionics technician to a task in ATA chapter 34. True or false?

generalfeedback.text: Navigation is ATA chapter 34. The readout gives the fault code and sends the technician to AMM 34-11-00 and to the IPC — the same cross-reference habit as chapter 32.

feedback.text: Correct — chapter 34 is navigation, and the readout points to AMM 34-11-00.
Read again — the fault code and the AMM reference are both in chapter 34.

questiontext.text:
Read the service bulletin summary.

SB 24-089 — Electrical Power. Status: Recommended. Applicability: aircraft MSN 0460 to 0475. Reason: improved generator control unit.

Which aircraft does SB 24-089 apply to?

generalfeedback.text: Always read the applicability (effectivity). This bulletin applies only to aircraft MSN 0460 to 0475, not to the whole fleet.

feedback.text: Correct — the applicability line names MSN 0460 to 0475.

answer.text: Every aircraft in the fleet without any exception

feedback.text: No — the applicability limits it to a range of MSNs.

answer.text: Only aircraft still fitted with the old nose wheel

feedback.text: No — that was SB 32-115; this bulletin is about electrical power.

answer.text: All aircraft listed under ATA chapter 32 only

feedback.text: No — SB 24-089 is chapter 24 (electrical power), and it names MSNs.

questiontext.text:
Complete with the present simple. Type one word.

The AMM ______ (list) every approved task.

generalfeedback.text: "The AMM" is one thing (it), so the verb takes the third-person -s: lists.

feedback.text: Correct — a singular subject takes the -s.
Use the present simple with the -s: lists.

questiontext.text:
Complete with the present simple. Type one word.

The two manuals ______ (cover) different systems.

generalfeedback.text: "The two manuals" is plural (they), so the verb takes no -s: cover.

feedback.text: Correct — a plural subject takes no -s.
A plural subject takes no -s: cover.

questiontext.text:
Make it a question. Type one word for the gap.

Statement: The effectivity matches your aircraft.

Question: ______ the effectivity match your aircraft?

generalfeedback.text: A present-simple question with a singular subject uses "Does" + subject + base verb: Does the effectivity match...?

feedback.text: Correct — Does + subject + base verb.
Use the auxiliary for a singular subject: Does.

questiontext.text:
Complete the negative present simple. Type the missing verb phrase.

A note ______ (not / order) you to stop.

generalfeedback.text: The negative present simple is does not + base verb: does not order. The -s moves onto "does".

feedback.text: Correct — does not + base verb.
Correct — the contracted form is fine.
Use does not + base verb: does not order.

questiontext.text:
Add the missing word. Type one word.

Read ______ effectivity before you start.

generalfeedback.text: English needs the article here: read the effectivity. Latvian and Russian have no articles, so it is easy to drop.

feedback.text: Correct — read the effectivity.
The noun needs an article: the.

questiontext.text:
Write the term from the unit.

The mandatory order from the authority, which you must obey, is the ______ .

generalfeedback.text: An airworthiness directive (AD) is a mandatory order from the authority. A service bulletin, by contrast, is usually only recommended.

feedback.text: Correct — an airworthiness directive is mandatory.
Correct — AD is the airworthiness directive.
The mandatory order is the airworthiness directive (AD).

questiontext.text:
Write the term (or its abbreviation) from the unit.

The publication that shows and numbers every part is the ______ .

generalfeedback.text: The IPC (Illustrated Parts Catalogue) shows and numbers every part. It shares chapter numbers with the AMM, so the two cross-reference.

feedback.text: Correct — the IPC.
Correct — the Illustrated Parts Catalogue (IPC).
It is the IPC, the Illustrated Parts Catalogue.

questiontext.text:
Rewrite the verb in the present simple (a permanent fact, not the continuous). Type one word.

Wrong: The chapter is covering the landing gear.

Right: The chapter ______ the landing gear.

generalfeedback.text: A permanent fact takes the present simple, not the continuous: the chapter covers the landing gear.

feedback.text: Correct — a fact takes the present simple: covers.
Use the present simple for a fact: covers.

questiontext.text: Match each document to what it does.

generalfeedback.text: Each publication has one clear job: the AMM gives the method, the IPC the parts, the MEL the go/no-go decision, the tech log the record, and the work order the instruction.

answer.text: lists the approved tasks and the steps
says whether the aircraft may fly
records the defects and the work done
is the instruction to do a job

questiontext.text: Match each term to its role.

generalfeedback.text: Warnings protect people; cautions protect the aircraft; notes only inform. An airworthiness directive is mandatory; a service bulletin is usually recommended.

answer.text: protects people from injury or death
a mandatory order you must obey
a recommended change from the maker

questiontext.text: Match each term to the verb it goes with.

generalfeedback.text: At B2 the word's company matters: you raise a work order, embody a service bulletin, comply with an airworthiness directive, follow a cross-reference and consult the MEL.

questiontext.text: Match each part of the numbering system to its meaning.

generalfeedback.text: The number reads left to right: chapter 32 is the landing gear, page block 401 is removal and installation, and 32-41-01 is the nose-wheel tyre task. Effectivity says which aircraft; a revision is a dated update.

answer.text: which aircraft a task applies to
a dated update to the manual
